nodes.norm_label: mesh curvature: knots equidistribute a curvature measure

nodes.norm_label: solver facts: factorisation dominates wall time

nodes.label: opts.ipopt.tol = 1e-8, acceptable_tol = 1e-6
nodes.rationale: Accuracy of the NLP solve (1e-8 standard); acceptable tolerance when tol cannot be reached (1e-6 standard).

nodes.label: circuit 'BowsersCastleN64': 45, 90 and 180 degree turns, 240 degree spiral and a long straight
nodes.norm_label: circuit 'bowserscastlen64': 45, 90 and 180 degree turns, 240 degree spiral and a long straight
nodes.rationale: Comments label each block: straight, 45/90/180 degree turns, spiral 240 degrees left (4/3 pi), final 90 degree right, back to start.

nodes.label: circuits 'Hairpin' and 'HairpinMirror': curvature +-0.0975 for 16 samples after 75 straight samples
nodes.norm_label: circuits 'hairpin' and 'hairpinmirror': curvature +-0.0975 for 16 samples after 75 straight samples

nodes.label: circuits 'Straight' and 'StraightMirror': zero curvature, 300 samples
nodes.rationale: StraightMirror is defined identically to Straight.

nodes.label: circuit 'Sturn': curvature +pi/45 then -pi/45 for 20 samples each, 30 straight samples between
nodes.norm_label: circuit 'sturn': curvature +pi/45 then -pi/45 for 20 samples each, 30 straight samples between

nodes.label: circuit 'VirtualTrack': mixed turns with a -pi/500*(1:0.05:6) curvature ramp
nodes.norm_label: circuit 'virtualtrack': mixed turns with a -pi/500*(1:0.05:6) curvature ramp

nodes.label: circuits 'ZigZag' and 'ZigZagMirror': hairpin pair then two 250-sample circle arcs
nodes.norm_label: circuits 'zigzag' and 'zigzagmirror': hairpin pair then two 250-sample circle arcs

nodes.label: vi = 60 m/s (initial speed)
nodes.rationale: Commented alternatives: 61.7428, 20, 0.1. Comments list AWD initial speeds per aero configuration.

nodes.label: Powertrain.m (script)
nodes.rationale: Two parallel e-motors: 228 kW and 301 Nm continuous each, 17750 rpm max (SPM242-176 helix). Gear ratio sized from the 290 km/h top speed.

nodes.label: pt.Pmax = 2*228 kW, pt.OMmax = 17750 rpm in rad/s, pt.eff = 0.9
nodes.norm_label: pt.pmax = 2*228 kw, pt.ommax = 17750 rpm in rad/s, pt.eff = 0.9

nodes.label: pt struct (powertrain ratings)
nodes.rationale: Five scalar ratings (Pmax, Tmax, OMmax, Vmax, eff), no power or rpm map. userOpts.m adds pt.ATD and pt.EM4 later.

nodes.label: vp.gear = pt.OMmax*vp.Rw/pt.Vmax (final drive ratio)
nodes.rationale: Final drive ratio based on the top speed requirement.

nodes.label: Guard: ATD and Electric_4Motors cannot both be On
nodes.norm_label: guard: atd and electric_4motors cannot both be on
nodes.rationale: If both are On, a warning is raised and ATD is forced Off while Electric_4Motors stays On.

nodes.label: duk_ub, duk_lb, ru, rdu, rdu2 assembled per pt.EM4, pt.ATD and vp.ActAero (12 branches)
nodes.norm_label: duk_ub, duk_lb, ru, rdu, rdu2 assembled per pt.em4, pt.atd and vp.actaero (12 branches)
nodes.rationale: Entry order follows the control vector in vehModel.m. No EM4=1 with ATD=1 branch because the guard forces ATD Off.

nodes.label: Active aero inputs by vp.ActAero: RW 0-30 deg; FW 0-10; FL, FR 0-10; TW -12 to 12
nodes.norm_label: active aero inputs by vp.actaero: rw 0-30 deg; fw 0-10; fl, fr 0-10; tw -12 to 12
nodes.rationale: Inputs join u, but the aero equations read static vp.alpha_FL, FR, RW, TW, so they do not reach the dynamics in this file.

nodes.label: ATD inputs: ATD_FL, ATD_FR, ATD_RL, ATD_RR wheel fractions in [0, 1]
nodes.norm_label: atd inputs: atd_fl, atd_fr, atd_rl, atd_rr wheel fractions in [0, 1]
nodes.rationale: Each input is the fraction going to one wheel; used when pt.ATD = 1.

nodes.label: u: normalised inputs ordered [motor torque(s), T_brake, ATD x4, aero angles, delta]
nodes.norm_label: u: normalised inputs ordered [motor torque(s), t_brake, atd x4, aero angles, delta]

nodes.label: nx = 23; nu = 3 to 11 (EM4 off) or 6 to 10 (EM4 on); ny = 0
nodes.norm_label: nx = 23; nu = 3 to 11 (em4 off) or 6 to 10 (em4 on); ny = 0
nodes.rationale: nu by config for ActAero 0 to 3: EM4 off ATD off 3, 4, 5, 7; ATD on 7, 8, 9, 11; EM4 on 6, 7, 8, 10.

nodes.label: EM4 on inputs: T_motor_fl, fr, rl, rr each [0, Tmax]
nodes.norm_label: em4 on inputs: t_motor_fl, fr, rl, rr each [0, tmax]
nodes.rationale: Four independent motors replace the single T_motor input. Comments for fr, rl and rr all say front left.

nodes.label: Axle torques T_f, T_r from gear, Tdist, brkB; Om_motor = Om_f/2*gear + Om_r/2*gear; P_motor = Tdrive*Om_motor
nodes.norm_label: axle torques t_f, t_r from gear, tdist, brkb; om_motor = om_f/2*gear + om_r/2*gear; p_motor = tdrive*om_motor

nodes.label: EM4 on: Om_motor_xx = Om_xx/gear; P_motor_xx = T_motor_xx*Om_motor_xx
nodes.norm_label: em4 on: om_motor_xx = om_xx/gear; p_motor_xx = t_motor_xx*om_motor_xx
nodes.rationale: Divides wheel speed by gear while the single-motor branch multiplies by gear. Opposite conventions make motor speed and power differ by gear squared; flag for review.

nodes.label: EM4 off: Om_motor = wheel speeds/4 * gear; P_motor = T_motor*Om_motor
nodes.norm_label: em4 off: om_motor = wheel speeds/4 * gear; p_motor = t_motor*om_motor

nodes.label: EM4 off inputs: single T_motor [0, Tmax] and T_brake [-Tbrake_max, 0]
nodes.norm_label: em4 off inputs: single t_motor [0, tmax] and t_brake [-tbrake_max, 0]

nodes.label: Wheel torques T_xx per config: single motor split by Tdist and brkB; ATD fractions; four motors
nodes.norm_label: wheel torques t_xx per config: single motor split by tdist and brkb; atd fractions; four motors

nodes.label: vp.brkB = 0.6766 (front brake force fraction)
nodes.rationale: Fraction of total brake force going to the front wheels.

nodes.label: vp.Rw = vp.Rw_r = vp.Rw_f = 0.355 m (overwrites Powertrain value)
nodes.norm_label: vp.rw = vp.rw_r = vp.rw_f = 0.355 m (overwrites powertrain value)

nodes.label: vp.Tdist = 0.7281 (rear drive torque fraction)
nodes.rationale: Fraction of total torque going to the rear wheels.

nodes.label: Rw/gear quirk: gear sized from Rw 0.3142857, Rw later reset to 0.355
nodes.norm_label: rw/gear quirk: gear sized from rw 0.3142857, rw later reset to 0.355
nodes.rationale: vehParams.m overwrites vp.Rw with 0.355 but never recomputes vp.gear, so the gear ratio keeps the old wheel radius.

nodes.label: AeroConfig = 'Static' sets vp.ActAero = 0 (Static 0, Active_RW 1, Active 2, AALB 3)
nodes.norm_label: aeroconfig = 'static' sets vp.actaero = 0 (static 0, active_rw 1, active 2, aalb 3)
nodes.rationale: Comment lists 'ActiveRW' but the switch case is 'Active_RW'. Static = fixed wings, Active_RW = active rear wing, Active = active front and rear, AALB = asymmetrical front plus tilt rear wing.

nodes.label: Regularisation (ru, rdu, rdu2): delta (0, 8, 15), ATD (0, 0, 1.5), FW (0, 0, 0.3), RW (0, 0, 0.9), TW (0.005, 0, 0.4), torques and brake 0; aux rdy = [0; 0], rdy2 = [1; 0]
nodes.norm_label: regularisation (ru, rdu, rdu2): delta (0, 8, 15), atd (0, 0, 1.5), fw (0, 0, 0.3), rw (0, 0, 0.9), tw (0.005, 0, 0.4), torques and brake 0; aux rdy = [0; 0], rdy2 = [1; 0]
nodes.rationale: Comment lists aux variables [ltx; lty_f; lty_r] but rdy and rdy2 have two entries. The init program uses only the first entry.

nodes.label: pt.Tmax = 2*301 = 602 Nm (max continuous torque)
nodes.rationale: Source comment writes 301kW for Tmax, but the value is a torque in Nm. It scales the motor torque input in vehModel.

nodes.label: pt.Vmax = 290/3.6 m/s (required top speed)
nodes.rationale: Required top speed, used for gear selection. vehModel also uses it as the upper speed bound.

nodes.label: dx: state derivatives along track distance divided by x_s; Lon_acc = dvx/sf, Lat_acc = dvy/sf
nodes.norm_label: dx: state derivatives along track distance divided by x_s; lon_acc = dvx/sf, lat_acc = dvy/sf
nodes.rationale: State derivatives vector is scaled to match the scaled states vector.

nodes.label: u = [Tdrive_n; Tbrake_n; delta_n] with scales pt.Tmax, vp.Tbrake_max, pi/8
nodes.norm_label: u = [tdrive_n; tbrake_n; delta_n] with scales pt.tmax, vp.tbrake_max, pi/8

nodes.label: x_min / x_max: vx [OPT_e, Vmax], vy +-10, r +-pi/2, n +-4 m, eps +-pi/4, Om [0, Vmax/Rw]
nodes.norm_label: x_min / x_max: vx [opt_e, vmax], vy +-10, r +-pi/2, n +-4 m, eps +-pi/4, om [0, vmax/rw]

nodes.label: u_min / u_max: T_motor [0, Tmax], T_brake [-Tbrake_max, 0], ATD [0, 1], delta [-1, 1]
nodes.norm_label: u_min / u_max: t_motor [0, tmax], t_brake [-tbrake_max, 0], atd [0, 1], delta [-1, 1]

nodes.label: u_s: T_motor_s = pt.Tmax, T_brake_s = vp.Tbrake_max, ATD 1, aero 10/30/12, delta_s
nodes.norm_label: u_s: t_motor_s = pt.tmax, t_brake_s = vp.tbrake_max, atd 1, aero 10/30/12, delta_s

nodes.label: kappa symbol (curvature, > 0 for left turns) and pv = kappa
nodes.norm_label: kappa symbol (curvature, > 0 for left turns) and pv = kappa
nodes.rationale: Not a decision variable; its value changes along the track, like a variable parameter.

nodes.label: sf = (1 - n*kappa)/(vx*cos(eps) - vy*sin(eps))
nodes.rationale: Change of independent variable from time to track distance.

nodes.label: x_min / x_max: vx [OPT_e, Vmax], vy +-10, r +-pi/2, n +-4 m, eps +-pi/4, zs +-0.1, theta +-0.1, phi +-0.09, zt [0, 0.1]
nodes.norm_label: x_min / x_max: vx [opt_e, vmax], vy +-10, r +-pi/2, n +-4 m, eps +-pi/4, zs +-0.1, theta +-0.1, phi +-0.09, zt [0, 0.1]
nodes.rationale: Constant track limits: lateral offset n bounded to +-4 m.

nodes.label: x_s: vx 100, vy 10, r 1, n 5, eps 1, Om_xx = 100/Rw, suspension states 1
nodes.norm_label: x_s: vx 100, vy 10, r 1, n 5, eps 1, om_xx = 100/rw, suspension states 1

nodes.label: Symbolic model: x, u, dx, sf, x_s, u_s, bounds, pv (base workspace variables)
nodes.norm_label: symbolic model: x, u, dx, sf, x_s, u_s, bounds, pv (base workspace variables)
nodes.rationale: MATLAB keeps the model as loose workspace variables. The Python port groups them in a model object (ctx.m23).

nodes.label: OPT_e = 1e-2 (small slack quantity)
nodes.rationale: Slack for the path constraints and wherever helpful, such as the solver initial guesses.

nodes.label: Normalised states and inputs: physical value = scale * normalised symbol
nodes.norm_label: normalised states and inputs: physical value = scale * normalised symbol
nodes.rationale: Each variable is a scaled SX symbol (vx_s = 100, n_s = 5 and so on); dx is divided by x_s at the end.

nodes.label: Space-domain ODE: derivatives taken along track distance via sf
nodes.norm_label: space-domain ode: derivatives taken along track distance via sf
nodes.rationale: Every state derivative is multiplied by sf, the change of independent variable.

nodes.label: Collocation setup: tau = collocation_points(OPT_d,'legendre'); [C,D,B] = collocation_coeff(tau)
nodes.rationale: Collocation points live in the normalised interval [0,1]. The linear maps C, D, B come from the CasADi collocation_coeff function.

nodes.label: Constraint vector g = [gb; gck; ghk; gduk] with bounds lbg, ubg
nodes.norm_label: constraint vector g = [gb; gck; ghk; gduk] with bounds lbg, ubg
nodes.rationale: Order is boundary conditions, collocation constraints, path constraints, rate of inputs. Collocation rows have zero bounds.

nodes.label: Discretisation grid: N, s_knot, dsk, s_col, s_full, curvature pv_knot/pv_col/pv_full
nodes.norm_label: discretisation grid: n, s_knot, dsk, s_col, s_full, curvature pv_knot/pv_col/pv_full
nodes.rationale: Xk has N+1 points but dsk has N. s_full interleaves knot and collocation points through Kronecker products, and curvature is interpolated from the track at each point.

nodes.label: CasADi functions f_dyn (dx, L) and f_sf (change of variable)
nodes.norm_label: casadi functions f_dyn (dx, l) and f_sf (change of variable)
nodes.rationale: Objective integrand is L = sf, the time per unit arc length. f_sf evaluates the change of variable so input rates can be converted back to time.

nodes.label: Discretisation grid: N, s_knot, dsk, s_col, s_full, pv_knot/pv_col/pv_full
nodes.norm_label: discretisation grid: n, s_knot, dsk, s_col, s_full, pv_knot/pv_col/pv_full

nodes.label: Input-rate constraints duk_t with duk_lb_init, duk_ub_init
nodes.norm_label: input-rate constraints duk_t with duk_lb_init, duk_ub_init
nodes.rationale: Same trick as MLTP.m: divide du/ds by sf to get du/dt. The init limits are divided by u_s inside vehModel_initial.m.

nodes.label: Input-rate constraints gduk = duk ./ Sfk (time derivative of inputs)
nodes.norm_label: input-rate constraints gduk = duk ./ sfk (time derivative of inputs)
nodes.rationale: Divides du/ds by sf to undo the change of independent variable: du/dt = du/ds * 1/sf = du/ds * ds/dt.

nodes.label: Transcription: collocation, discretisation, loop and objective with aux Yk and P argument
nodes.norm_label: transcription: collocation, discretisation, loop and objective with aux yk and p argument
nodes.rationale: Same scheme as MLTP.m. The loop passes P to f_dyn and the objective adds first and second derivative penalties on the aux variables Yk.

nodes.label: OPT_d = 3 (degree of interpolating polynomials, set in userOpts.m)
nodes.norm_label: opt_d = 3 (degree of interpolating polynomials, set in useropts.m)

nodes.label: OPT_ds = 10 m (collocation step, set in userOpts.m)
nodes.norm_label: opt_ds = 10 m (collocation step, set in useropts.m)
nodes.rationale: The Python port documents a default step of 30 m, so the two codebases differ in default mesh density.

nodes.label: Direct Legendre collocation
nodes.rationale: Legendre points of degree OPT_d on each interval. The polynomial derivative must match the system dynamics at the collocation points (defect constraints), with end-state continuity between intervals.

nodes.label: Input-rate limits divided by the input scale (duk_lb, duk_ub over u_s)
nodes.norm_label: input-rate limits divided by the input scale (duk_lb, duk_ub over u_s)
nodes.rationale: userOpts.m gives limits per second in physical units (delta 0.1 rad/s). vehModel.m divides them by u_s, so they match duk_t, the time derivative of the normalised inputs.

nodes.label: Space-domain transcription (independent variable s, change of variable sf)
nodes.norm_label: space-domain transcription (independent variable s, change of variable sf)
nodes.rationale: Independent variable is track arc length s. Dynamics are multiplied by sf = dt/ds and the lap time is the integral of sf ds, so L = sf.

nodes.label: c struct (input rate limits ub/lb and regularisation ru, rdu, rdu2)
nodes.norm_label: c struct (input rate limits ub/lb and regularisation ru, rdu, rdu2)

nodes.label: duk_ub / duk_lb input rate bound vectors (per second)
nodes.norm_label: duk_ub / duk_lb input rate bound vectors (per second)

nodes.label: duk_ub_init, duk_lb_init, ru_init, rdu_init, rdu2_init, rdy_init, rdy2_init (init program)
nodes.norm_label: duk_ub_init, duk_lb_init, ru_init, rdu_init, rdu2_init, rdy_init, rdy2_init (init program)
nodes.rationale: Rate constraints and regularisation for the initialisation program, u = [Tdrive_n; T_brake_n; delta_n].

nodes.label: delta_s = pi/8 steering scale, delta_lim = [-pi/4, pi/4]/delta_s
nodes.norm_label: delta_s = pi/8 steering scale, delta_lim = [-pi/4, pi/4]/delta_s
nodes.rationale: Only definition of delta_s among these files; vehModel.m uses it without defining it.

nodes.label: duk_ub = duk_ub./u_s; duk_lb = duk_lb./u_s
nodes.rationale: Input rate bounds from userOpts.m are divided by the input scales.

nodes.label: delta = delta_max*delta_n with delta_max = 35 deg (0.611 rad), delta_lim = [-1, 1]
nodes.norm_label: delta = delta_max*delta_n with delta_max = 35 deg (0.611 rad), delta_lim = [-1, 1]
nodes.rationale: Desired max steering angle in degrees, normalised control input.

nodes.label: Rate limits: T_motor +-2e4 Nm/s (also per corner), T_brake +-1.45e5 Nm/s, ATD +-2e4 1/s
nodes.norm_label: rate limits: t_motor +-2e4 nm/s (also per corner), t_brake +-1.45e5 nm/s, atd +-2e4 1/s

nodes.label: Rate limits: FW +-20, RW +-60, TW +-24 deg/s
nodes.norm_label: rate limits: fw +-20, rw +-60, tw +-24 deg/s

nodes.label: Steering rate scale pi/8 (delta_s used in u_s, defined only in vehModel_initial.m)
nodes.norm_label: steering rate scale pi/8 (delta_s used in u_s, defined only in vehmodel_initial.m)
nodes.rationale: delta_s is defined only in vehModel_initial.m (pi/8). Full vehModel.m uses it in u_s to scale rate bounds, yet scales steering by delta_max = 35 deg. Relies on base-workspace leakage.

nodes.label: Path constraints h, nh = 6 (front and rear friction circle, motor power, motor rpm, ltx_eq, BrTh)
nodes.norm_label: path constraints h, nh = 6 (front and rear friction circle, motor power, motor rpm, ltx_eq, brth)
nodes.rationale: Lumped front and rear friction circles mu_lim_f and mu_lim_r replace the per-wheel rows. ltx_eq keeps the load transfer aux variable consistent. A shorter constraint set is commented out.

nodes.label: Path constraints h, nh = 9 or 10 (per-wheel friction circle, motor, ltx_eq, lty_eq, BrTh_1, ATD_eq)
nodes.norm_label: path constraints h, nh = 9 or 10 (per-wheel friction circle, motor, ltx_eq, lty_eq, brth_1, atd_eq)
nodes.rationale: Load-transfer equalities ltx_eq and lty_eq are active here, unlike in MLTP.m where they are commented out.

nodes.label: Constraint count check nh vs length(h) (CombinedSlip 3/12/4 rows, PureSlip 7/16/8 rows)
nodes.norm_label: constraint count check nh vs length(h) (combinedslip 3/12/4 rows, pureslip 7/16/8 rows)
nodes.rationale: Raises 'Number of path constraints of the OCP is not consistent' when nh differs from length(h).

nodes.label: Path constraints h with bounds h_lb, h_ub (brake-throttle overlap, motor power and rpm, ATD_eq, friction circle)
nodes.norm_label: path constraints h with bounds h_lb, h_ub (brake-throttle overlap, motor power and rpm, atd_eq, friction circle)
nodes.rationale: Load-transfer equalities ltx_eq and lty_eq are commented out in this model. The row set changes with pt.EM4, pt.ATD and TyreModel.

nodes.label: SDI timeseries logging into data.sdi (states, inputs, track, vehicle, constraints)
nodes.norm_label: sdi timeseries logging into data.sdi (states, inputs, track, vehicle, constraints)
nodes.rationale: States and inputs are logged on the s_full axis, vehicle channels on s_knot. Vehicle parameters are stored as constant series just to record the values used for each simulation.

nodes.label: Friction-circle rows mu_lim_* use fz / vp.Fz0_shift
nodes.norm_label: friction-circle rows mu_lim_* use fz / vp.fz0_shift
nodes.rationale: Normal load is divided by the shift inside the friction-circle rows, which ties the tyre load scaling to the design variable.

nodes.label: Signal selection with getSignalsByName(data.sdi.run, name) and plotOnSubPlot
nodes.norm_label: signal selection with getsignalsbyname(data.sdi.run, name) and plotonsubplot
nodes.rationale: Subplots: velocity, steering and lateral speed; torques; slip angles and ratios; wheel speeds; side force and lift per wheel; tyre fx, fy, fz per wheel.

nodes.label: Friction-circle rows per TyreModel (CombinedSlip: none; PureSlip: rho_lim_fl/fr/rl/rr)
nodes.norm_label: friction-circle rows per tyremodel (combinedslip: none; pureslip: rho_lim_fl/fr/rl/rr)
nodes.rationale: CombinedSlip adds no friction-circle rows. PureSlip adds rho_lim = sqrt((fx/(mu_x fz))^2 + (fy/(mu_y fz))^2) per wheel, bounded to [0,1].

nodes.label: Figure: tyre force points against friction circles (FrictionCircles.fig)
nodes.norm_label: figure: tyre force points against friction circles (frictioncircles.fig)
nodes.rationale: Plots fx/(mu_x*fz) against fy/(mu_y*fz) per wheel against a unit circle, reading mu and force series from data.sdi.vehicle.

nodes.label: IPOPT options struct opts (built in userOpts.m, passed to nlpsol)
nodes.norm_label: ipopt options struct opts (built in useropts.m, passed to nlpsol)
nodes.rationale: opts is built in userOpts.m and handed to nlpsol unchanged. Print level, linear solver and stats options are not set here.

nodes.label: NLP creation: nlp = struct('f',J,'x',w,'g',g); solver = nlpsol('solver','ipopt',nlp,opts)
nodes.norm_label: nlp creation: nlp = struct('f',j,'x',w,'g',g); solver = nlpsol('solver','ipopt',nlp,opts)

nodes.label: IPOPT fixed_variable_treatment = 'make_constraint'
nodes.rationale: Comment: with default options multipliers for decision variables are wrong for equality constraints; make_constraint or relax_bounds fixes this per CasADi docs. No difference observed in the solution or solver when disabled.

nodes.label: IPOPT linear_solver not set in opts (solver default applies)
nodes.norm_label: ipopt linear_solver not set in opts (solver default applies)
nodes.rationale: No linear_solver option appears in userOpts.m or MLTP.m. The Python port selects ma57 with a MUMPS fallback.

nodes.label: IPOPT mu_init = 1e-1 (initial barrier parameter)
nodes.rationale: userOpts.m comment: initial value of the barrier parameter, 1e-1 standard.

nodes.label: IPOPT print_level and print_time not set in opts (solver defaults apply)
nodes.norm_label: ipopt print_level and print_time not set in opts (solver defaults apply)
nodes.rationale: No print option appears in userOpts.m or MLTP.m, so console output follows the IPOPT and CasADi defaults.

nodes.label: IPOPT tolerances: tol 1e-8, acceptable_tol 1e-6, constr_viol_tol 1e-4, dual_inf_tol 1e-4, compl_inf_tol 1e-4, bound_push 1e-2, bound_frac 1e-2
nodes.norm_label: ipopt tolerances: tol 1e-8, acceptable_tol 1e-6, constr_viol_tol 1e-4, dual_inf_tol 1e-4, compl_inf_tol 1e-4, bound_push 1e-2, bound_frac 1e-2
nodes.rationale: Every value matches the standard quoted in the userOpts.m comments.
